instruction: I need to use an on-screen keyboard because my physical keyboard isn't working well. Please enable the virtual keyboard on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: OSK_ENABLED=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-keyboard-enabled 2>/dev/null | grep -c true); if [ "$OSK_ENABLED" -gt 0 ]; then echo "On-screen keyboard enabled"; else echo "On-screen keyboard not enabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling on-screen keyboard via Settings > Accessibility > Typing > Screen Keyboard. Evaluator checks screen-keyboard-enabled setting. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks the GNOME accessibility setting 'org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-keyboard-enabled' which directly controls the on-screen keyboard feature
The vm_command_line getter with shell command is the appropriate method to query gsettings for system configuration state
The check_include_exclude metric correctly validates the output by ensuring 'On-screen keyboard enabled' is present and 'On-screen keyboard not enabled' and 'error' are absent
The shell command has proper error handling with timeout (10s) and stderr redirection (2>/dev/null)
Expected values match the actual output the command will produce, ensuring correct verification
Complete coverage: The evaluator checks the exact requirement stated in the instruction - whether the virtual/on-screen keyboard is enabled
No postconfig needed since gsettings is a persistent configuration that can be queried at any time without reopening UI dialogs
